None of the three solutions is correct. The correct answer is 1.

- $f(2)=6$, so $f^{-1}(6)=2$.
- $f(1)=2$, so $f^{-1}(2)=1$.
- Therefore $f^{-1}(f^{-1}(6))=f^{-1}(2)=1$.

Solution 1 invents a linear model for $f^{-1}$ from two points and gets 10. Solution 2 finds $f^{-1}(6)=2$ but stops before applying $f^{-1}$ a second time, giving 2. Solution 3 wrongly takes $f^{-1}(2)$ to be $f(2)=6$, confusing $f^{-1}(2)$ with $f(2)$, and gets 6.

CHOICE: NONE
